newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile snow-hit El Teniente mine returns to normal.
newsitem.headline: Chile snow-hit El Teniente mine returns to normal.

text.p: Chilean state copper company Codelco's El Teniente mine expects to operate as usual Tuesday after heavy weekend snowfall forced the closure of its concentrator and mill, said a division spokesman.
"We expect everything to be operating completely normally today," said Rodrigo Rivas by telephone from Rancagua.
Workers have been able to return to the mine and the concentrator has begun operations again, he said.
Trains bringing mineral out from the underground pit are not yet operating because of problems within the mine, said Rivas. He did not know the cause of the difficulties.
The Caletones smelter has continued operating despite the snow by using stockpiles of mineral mined at El Teniente and Codelco's nearby Andina pit.
Production at El Teniente, Codelco's second largest division, was disrupted Saturday after a violent blizzard dumped over two meters of snow cutting access roads to the pit.
Rivas said it was too early to say what impact the bad weather had on production at the pit which mined 345,000 tonnes of copper last year.
